relevance_note: Cross-sectional ultrasound study of 10 individually tabulated Blau syndrome patients with NOD2 mutations: 'All patients had been shown to have a known NOD2 gene mutation associated with Blau syndrome'.
method_note: A Python script in my scratch directory transcribed Table 1 and Table 2 cells (typed by hand from the paper and checked: every span verified verbatim against the paper; the paper uses non-breaking spaces between numbers and units, which the spans keep). Labels: the text refers to patients as 'patient N' (Table 1 'Patient number' 1-10, numbered by age), so rule 1 gives 'patient 1'..'patient 10'. Patients 5 and 6 have two Table 1/Table 2 rows (1st and 2nd ultrasound examination); age at last evaluation uses the 2nd examination; Table 1/2 ages are in months per the 'Age (months)' header. Family: 'Patients 1, 2, and 10 were offspring and a parent' and 'the siblings (patients 1 and 2)': patient 10 is the parent of patients 1 and 2, sex not stated; no family labels; 'Ten patients (two female)' but which two is not stated (patients 3 and 6 male from 'He'/'his'). Patient 2 is previously reported in ref [34], whose title mentions 'a 5-year-old boy'; I did not use a reference title to set sex. Inheritance for patients 1 and 2 recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' because the parent (patient 10) carries the same R334W per Table 1 and the text; patient 10's own inheritance not reported. Variant type 'missense' for R334W/R334Q only from the Introduction sentence naming them as mis-sense mutations; D382E and R587C have no stated class. Pathogenicity from the group statement 'All patients had been shown to have a known NOD2 gene mutation associated with Blau syndrome'. Phenotypes: Table 1 'At onset of joint symptom' / 'At onset of skin lesion' / 'At diagnosis of uveitis' ages recorded as feature onsets; NA ('not applicable') cells treated as not reported; individual-level age at onset left 'not reported' because the paper gives only per-feature ages. 'Skin lesion' was mapped to the checklist item 'granulomatous dermatitis or skin rash'; 'joint symptom' onset mapped to 'arthritis or joint synovitis' (the Table 1 note equates it with 'arthritic symptoms'). ESR/CRP: elevated/not elevated judged by comparing each Table 2 value with the normal range printed in the same cell (header 'Acute inflammatory response (normal range^§)'); patient 1 CRP 3.0 sits exactly at the upper limit (0 to 3) and was taken as within range. MMP-3, DAS28, VAS and CHAQ values not extracted as features. Tender/swollen joint counts are per-patient values (not group counts); a count of 0/40 recorded as 'excluded' for tender or swollen joints only, never for the broader arthritis checklist item. Bursitis: 'Bursitis was identified only in ... one patient (patient 6)' with all patients assessed, so bursitis recorded excluded for the other nine (inferred from group statement). Patient 3 arthritis taken from the Discussion ('severity of arthritis in patient 3 (D382E) and 4 (R587C)') although Table 1 joint-symptom onset is NA. Ultrasound heat maps (Figures 1 and 2) are images only; per-patient tenosynovitis recorded only where the text names the patient (2, 5, 6). The ranges 'severe cases ... clustered between patient 5 and patient 8' were not assigned to individuals. Contradictions/discrepancies in the paper: (1) patient 3 is cited as 'ref [36]' in Table 1 but the text cites [39] (a case report of infantile Takayasu arteritis with p.D382E), while [36] is an RA ultrasound paper; both recorded in source_reference_in_review. (2) Patient 8 is 212 months (17 years 8 months) in Table 1 but '18 years and 8 months old' in the text; Table 1 value used. (3) Patient 2: Table 1 NSAID 'NA' but the text says 'receiving an NSAID and methotrexate'. (4) Patient 10 'reported no arthritic symptoms' (Table 1 note) yet has swollen joint count 3/28 and 5/40 in Table 2; both recorded (arthritic symptoms excluded; swollen joints observed), and the checklist arthritis item set observed from the swollen joints, since history of symptoms and examined swelling are different features. Ten age- and sex-matched control subjects are out of scope and get no rows.
